Alice — thank you and the MedAlign team for the quick turnaround.

Short answers up front:
- BYOK handover: Customer provisions keys into the tenant keystore during staging (pre-prod) and we do not store plaintext key material. We can support a KMS-handoff flow (customer creates CMK in their KMS and grants access via a one-time wrapped key). No mandatory escrow from Redwood, but we can sign an addendum for escrow under specific contractual conditions.
- Egress: For Private deployments we will enforce VPC-level egress controls by default; we can document allowed endpoints and audits.

I'm looping in Karthik (legal/integration) and Irene (solutions) for technical specifics and a proposed redline counter. We'll review the PDF and come back with suggested language by EOD Friday.

Next steps:
1) Karthik: can you confirm whether the addendum for escrow needs to be present now or can be a post-signature annex?
2) Irene: please advise the minimal network egress statement we can commit to for MedAlign's compliance review.

Best,

Maya — quick legal perspective:

1) Escrow addendum: We prefer escrow as an optional annex that can be invoked under defined events (catastrophic loss, long-term discontinuation). For enterprise deals we have precedent to draft an escrow schedule tied to a custody protocol rather than baking escrow into the main DPA. Suggest: "Escrow: available by written request; schedule and terms in Annex X."

2) Key custody wording: propose the following short clause for the DPA redline: "Customer retains sole control of cryptographic keys (BYOK). Redwood will not possess or persist plaintext key material and will only store wrapped keys or key references required for runtime. Operational access to keystore management interfaces will be limited to named Redwood operators under break-glass procedures and logged with SIEM export to customer-controlled logging endpoint."

3) Export controls / egress: Legal is neutral on listing endpoints; prefer a technical appendix (maintained outside main DPA) that enumerates allowed egress endpoints and audit controls so it can be updated without reopening the DPA.

Laura — can you weigh in on the SIEM/logging export feasibility and any latency/throughput impacts?

-Karthik
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy

Folks — technical notes / proposed minimal commitments for the appendix:

- BYOK handoff flow: customer supplies a wrapped key blob (RSA-wrapped or KMS-wrapped) into the tenant keystore during onboarding. We support AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault integrations and a raw wrapped-key ingestion API for on-prem HSMs. We will document the supported wrapping algorithms in the appendix.

- Operator access and break-glass: Redwood operators will have a named service account model for emergency key access. Access is gated by an approval flow (two approvers: Escalations on-call + SOC lead) and each break-glass event generates a signed audit bundle delivered to customer's secure bucket.

- Egress / endpoints: For MedAlign we can commit to blocking all outbound connections except:
  * Customer telemetry sink (customer.s3.amazonaws.com),
  * Redwood license/heartbeat endpoints (r-inf-heartbeat.redwood.com),
  * Optional registry for model updates if requested (models.redwood.com) — this one can be disabled.

- Evidence: we can provide sample SIEM export (syslog over TLS) and a sanitized network topology (see attached network_topology_v2.png).

If that set of controls looks good to MedAlign, Karthik can convert into contract language and I will add the technical appendix content.

— Irene
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Alice / Bob — putting the proposed approach together in one place:

1) BYOK: Customer retains key ownership. Onboarding flow will ingest a wrapped key; Redwood will not retain plaintext. Optional escrow is available as Annex X (invoked post-signature).

2) Operator access: Break-glass is allowed only under a documented two-approver flow; a signed audit bundle will be delivered to your secure bucket immediately after any event.

3) Egress: By default outbound traffic is blocked except for your telemetry sink and mandatory heartbeat. Model update registry is opt-in and can be disabled for MedAlign.

Next actions:
- MedAlign: confirm whether you prefer the escrow annex to be included in the executed agreement or as a post-signature deliverable.
- Redwood (Karthik): will draft the short contract clauses and the technical appendix (Irene) and circulate by Tue EOD.
